source_spans.locator: Science 275(5306), published p.1593, Abstract/opening: learning is related to changes in expectations about future salient events; primate midbrain cell output is interpreted as signaling changes or errors in those expectations

Science 275(5306), published p.1594, 'Information Encoded in Dopaminergic Activity' and Fig. 1: phasic response shifts from delivered outcome to predictive cue with training; omission produces a timed below-baseline response; positive/zero/negative deviations are distinguished
Science 275(5306), published p.1595, 'Computational Theory and Model', Eqs. 1-3: discounted future-value target and successive-time signed discrepancy δ(t)=r(t)+γVhat(t+1)-Vhat(t)

Science 275(5306), published p.1595, stimulus-through-time representation and Eqs. 4-5: cue traces and adaptable weights form the value estimate; weight change depends on cue activity, signed discrepancy, and learning rate

Science 275(5306), published pp.1595-1596, Fig. 2 and model-data comparison: reward-value input and temporal change in ongoing value estimate are combined; midbrain output is modeled as the signed discrepancy plus baseline and broadcast to structures constructing the estimate so it can control plasticity
Science 275(5306), published p.1596, Fig. 3 and surrounding text: training shifts the model transient to the earliest consistent cue and omitted expected events produce a timed negative fluctuation

conditions: appetitive cue-outcome conditioning with repeated training
comparison of unforecast, accurately forecast, and omitted expected outcomes
computational interpretation using successive-time value estimates and adaptable cue weights
population: alert nonhuman primates in single-unit recording experiments
substrate: midbrain dopaminergic cell populations in ventral tegmental area and substantia nigra
temporal_scope: successive time steps within a trial
the expected time of outcome delivery after cue onset

nodes.description: time-indexed representation of a sensory cue across successive steps after cue onset
value of the appetitive outcome available at the current time step, including zero when an expected outcome is omitted
current estimate of the discounted sum of future appetitive outcomes
estimate of discounted future appetitive outcomes at the next time step
factor between zero and one that discounts outcomes arriving later in time
successive-time signed discrepancy formed from current outcome value, discounted next-step estimate, and current estimate
transient increase, absence of change, or decrease in firing of the recorded midbrain dopaminergic cell population
adjustable weights linking time-indexed cue components to the current future-value estimate
trial-to-trial change in adaptive cue weights determined from cue activity and the signed discrepancy signal
cue-specific scalar controlling the size of the adaptive weight change
repeated temporal pairing of sensory cues followed by appetitive outcome delivery
comparison among unforecast outcome delivery, correctly forecast delivery, and omission at the expected time

relations.description: the current future-value estimate is constructed from the time-indexed cue representation and its adaptive weights
the signed successive-time discrepancy is determined by current outcome value plus the discounted next-step estimate minus the current estimate

the source models the transient midbrain output as reflecting the signed successive-time discrepancy, with positive, near-zero, and negative deviations corresponding to better-than-forecast, as-forecast, and worse-than-forecast events
the adaptive weight change depends on cue activity, the signed discrepancy, and a cue-specific learning-rate factor
the update operation changes the cue-associated weights from one trial to the next
across repeated cue-outcome training, the timing of the transient output shifts from outcome delivery toward the earliest consistent predictive cue
the outcome-delivery and omission comparisons expose positive, near-zero, and negative transient-output patterns at the relevant times
the conditioned sensory cue precedes the later outcome time represented within the trial
